description: Lineage of modern U.S. national forests with western/AK/PR scope plus eastern forests with pre-March-4-1909 roots, and year-by-year forest reserve totals under Theodore Roosevelt.

field_notes.origin: Strict per spec: classification of the EARLIEST predecessor reserve whose land is (or is believed to be) inside the modern forest. pre-TR = proclaimed before 1901-09-14; TR = 1901-09-14..1909-03-04; post-TR after; 'uncertain' where not resolvable.
field_notes.primary_origin: Recommended for map coloring: classification of the core/namesake reserve. Differs from origin where a small fragment came from an older reserve (mixed_lineage=true).
field_notes.first_tr_year: Year TR first proclaimed land now in this forest (for TR-origin) or first enlarged it (for pre-TR); null if none known.
field_notes.tr_enlarged: Pre-TR forests only: did TR add land to the predecessor reserve (yes/no/unknown). Many TR proclamations both added and deleted land; 'yes' means at least one documented addition, not a verified net gain.
field_notes.confidence: high = direct FS-612 chain; medium = chain partly inferred; low = depends on unverified parcel transfers.
field_notes.dates: Proclamation (approval) dates from FS-612; several 1897 and 1908 documents have different effective dates (asterisked in FS-612).

units.primary_predecessor: Big Hole (1906) and Hell Gate (1905) reserves via EO 877, Jul 1 1908
units.note: Created Jul 1 1908 from parts of Big Hole and Hell Gate; Madison NF land (Madison FR 1902) added Dec 16 1931. FS-612 also shows a 1946 transfer from Gallatin NF (Gallatin FR 1899 lineage) - whether that parcel was originally 1899 reserve land is unverified.

units.primary_predecessor: Hell Gate Forest Reserve (via Deerlodge, EO 880)
units.note: Established Jul 1 1908 from parts of Hell Gate (1905), Big Hole (1906) and Helena; Madison and Missoula NF lands added Dec 16 1931. All known predecessors TR-proclaimed.
Washington's Birthday reserve. TR deleted land Jun 14 1904, added/deleted May 22 1905, and on Jul 1 1908 added lands from TR-proclaimed Big Hole and Hell Gate reserves. Selway NF lands added 1934.

units.earliest_reserve: Cave Hills and Slim Buttes Forest Reserves
units.note: Otter FR (a Mar 2 1907 'midnight' proclamation) renamed Custer 1908. Sioux NF (Cave Hills 1904, Slim Buttes 1904, Short Pine 1905, Ekalaka 1906, Long Pine 1906) merged 1920. Beartooth district via Beartooth NF (1908, from Yellowstone FR Montana lands = former Absaroka FR 1902, plus Pryor Mtns FR 1906) in 1932. Original 1891 Yellowstone Park Timber Land Reserve was Wyoming-only per FS-612. Admin unit combined with Gallatin 2014 (verify date). Dakota Prairie Grasslands are separate (not proclaimed NF).
TR added land Mar 7 1906 and Jul 1 1908 (from Big Belt, TR 1905). Absaroka NF (Absaroka FR Sep 4 1902, TR) merged Dec 18 1945; part of Beartooth NF 1932.

units.primary_predecessor: Flathead Forest Reserve / Lewis & Clarke FR
units.note: Flathead FR consolidated into Lewis & Clarke FR Jun 9 1903 (boundary re-described), which TR enlarged again Mar 2 1907; Flathead NF re-established from it Jul 1 1908. Part of Blackfeet NF (also L&C lineage) added 1935. Whether the specific 1903/1907 additions fall inside today's Flathead (vs. Lewis and Clark NF) is not resolved here.

units.earliest_reserve: Lewis & Clarke Forest Reserve (via Blackfeet NF lands added 1935)
units.note: Core is Kootenai FR (Aug 13 1906, TR) plus Cabinet FR (Mar 2 1907, TR; abolished 1954 and divided among Kaniksu, Kootenai, Lolo). Blackfeet NF (carved Jun 25 1908 from Lewis & Clark, a 1897 reserve) was divided between Flathead and Kootenai Jun 22 1935, so a strict 'earliest predecessor' is 1897. For mapping, treat primary origin as TR.

units.earliest_reserve: Lewis & Clarke Forest Reserve (via 1931 transfer from Lewis & Clark NF)
units.note: Helena FR Apr 12 1906; Elkhorn FR (May 12 1905) and part of Big Belt (Oct 3 1905) combined into Helena Jul 1 1908. FS-612 records transfers into Helena from Gallatin (1912; Gallatin FR 1899) and Lewis & Clark (Dec 16 1931; L&C FR 1897) - whether those parcels were original pre-1901 reserve land is unverified. Primary origin TR.

TR re-described/enlarged it Jun 9 1903 (absorbing Flathead) and added land Mar 2 1907 (midnight reserves; spelling changed to Lewis & Clark). Jefferson NF (from Little Belt Mtns 1902, Highwood Mtns 1903, Snowy Mtns 1906, Little Rockies 1907 - all TR) merged Apr 8 1932 = today's Jefferson Division.

units.earliest_reserve: Bitter Root Forest Reserve (via later transfers from Bitterroot, Selway, Clearwater NFs)
units.primary_predecessor: Lolo FR (1906) and Missoula FR (1906, incl. Hell Gate 1905 lands)
units.note: Lolo FR Sep 20 1906; Missoula NF (Nov 6 1906 plus Hell Gate lands 1908) merged 1931; Cabinet (1907) part 1954. FS-612 shows parcels moving in from Bitterroot (1912, 1931), Selway (1934) and Clearwater (1935) - Bitter Root 1897 lineage. Primary origin TR.

units.primary_predecessor: Bitter Root Forest Reserve (Clearwater carved Jul 1 1908)
units.note: Created Jul 1 1908 from the Idaho part of Bitter Root FR. TR's May 22 1905 Bitter Root additions may lie here - unverified. Selway NF (1911) lands added 1934.

units.primary_predecessor: Bitter Root Forest Reserve (Nezperce carved Jun 26 1908)
units.note: Established Jun 26 1908 (EO 854) from Bitter Root lands; also received Weiser (1905, TR) land. Whether TR additions are inside today's boundary is unverified.
Also absorbed Palouse FR (Mar 2 1907) in 1908 and part of Pend Oreille NF (1933). Pend Oreille drew on Priest River FR (1897), so a small pre-TR fragment is possible but unverified.

TR added land to Priest River Nov 6 1906 and Mar 2 1907; Kaniksu formed Jun 26 1908 from Priest River. Most of Pend Oreille NF merged 1933; part of Cabinet (1907) 1954. Its Washington (Sullivan Lake) portion was later administered by Colville NF.

units.earliest_reserve: Bitter Root Forest Reserve (via Clearwater NF portion, 1911)
units.note: Established Jun 29 1911 (Taft) from parts of Coeur d'Alene (TR 1906) and Clearwater (Bitter Root 1897 lineage). Which share is larger is not determined here.

units.admin_unit: Arapaho and Roosevelt National Forests and Pawnee National Grassland
units.earliest_reserve: Uncertain: Pikes Peak FR lands (1905 consolidation of 1892 Pikes Peak, Plum Creek and South Platte TLRs)
units.primary_predecessor: Pikes Peak FR (1905) and Leadville FR (1905) lands via EO 888/893, Jul 1 1908
units.note: Established Jul 1 1908 from Pikes Peak FR and Leadville FR lands; later received Holy Cross and Leadville (1930), Pike and Roosevelt (1936), Routt (1946). Pikes Peak FR of 1905 combined three 1892 Harrison reserves plus new TR land; whether any original 1892 acreage ended up in Arapaho is unverified. Treat as TR for mapping, flag for verification.

units.admin_unit: Arapaho and Roosevelt National Forests and Pawnee National Grassland
units.earliest_reserve: Medicine Bow Forest Reserve (Colorado portion added May 17 1905)
units.primary_predecessor: Medicine Bow FR, Colorado division (renamed Colorado NF Jul 1 1910; Roosevelt NF Mar 28 1932)
units.note: Medicine Bow FR was proclaimed May 22 1902 in Wyoming; its Colorado lands were added May 17 1905 and Mar 2 1907. Renamed for Theodore Roosevelt in 1932. FS-612 also notes a 1917 transfer from Pike NF (Pike lineage includes 1892 reserves) - unverified whether original 1892 land.
McKinley added land 1900 and deleted 1901; TR added land May 22 1902 and added/deleted Dec 23 1904. Renamed Bighorn 1908.

TR deleted land Oct 31 1905 but proclaimed Bear Lodge FR (WY) Mar 1 1907; Bear Lodge + part of Black Hills became Sundance NF 1908, returned to Black Hills 1915 (today's Bearlodge district). Harney NF (1911) folded back 1954.

units.admin_unit: Grand Mesa, Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Forests
units.note: Under TR: land deleted 1901-1904, boundary re-described May 16 1904, land added AND deleted Jun 5 1905 (net effect not determined). Renamed Battlement NF 1908, Grand Mesa 1924. Fruita division (Fruita FR 1906, TR) transferred in 1921.

units.admin_unit: Grand Mesa, Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Forests
units.note: Later absorbed parts of Cochetopa NF (Cochetopah FR 1905) and Leadville (1905).

units.admin_unit: Grand Mesa, Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Forests
units.note: Absorbed Ouray FR (1907) 1908 and part of Montezuma NF (1905) 1947.

units.admin_unit: Medicine Bow-Routt National Forests and Thunder Basin National Grassland
units.earliest_reserve: Crow Creek Forest Reserve (probable, via 1925 addition from Fort F.E. Warren)
units.note: Medicine Bow FR proclaimed May 22 1902 by TR. Crow Creek FR (Oct 10 1900, McKinley) was merged into Cheyenne NF 1908; its division went to the War Department 1910, and FS-612 records land added to Medicine Bow from Fort Francis E. Warren Jun 5 1925 (likely today's Pole Mountain unit) - verify. Hayden NF (Sierra Madre 1906 / Park Range 1905) lands added 1929. Treat primary origin as TR.

units.admin_unit: Medicine Bow-Routt National Forests and Thunder Basin National Grassland
units.primary_predecessor: Park Range Forest Reserve (Routt est. Jun 25 1908)
units.note: Part of Hayden NF added 1929; small Colorado NF transfer 1930.

units.admin_unit: Pike and San Isabel National Forests and Cimarron and Comanche National Grasslands
units.primary_predecessor: Pikes Peak / Plum Creek / South Platte Timber Land Reserves (1892)
units.note: TR added/deleted land in South Platte Dec 6 1904 and on May 12 1905 consolidated the three 1892 reserves with new land as Pikes Peak FR; renamed Pike Jul 1 1908.

units.admin_unit: Pike and San Isabel National Forests and Cimarron and Comanche National Grasslands
units.note: Wet Mountains FR (1905) added 1908; part of Las Animas (1907) 1910.

units.earliest_reserve: San Juan / Cochetopah Forest Reserves (Rio Grande est. Jul 1 1908, EO 887)
units.primary_predecessor: Rio Grande NF (EO 887) from TR-proclaimed reserves
units.note: Exact parent reserves of EO 887 not itemized in FS-612 extract; all candidate parents (San Juan Jun 3 1905, Cochetopah Jun 13 1905) were TR proclamations.
Montezuma FR (Jun 13 1905) merged 1947; Durango NF (1911) returned 1920.

units.primary_predecessor: Yellowstone Park Timber Land Reserve (first U.S. forest reserve)
units.note: TR renamed it Yellowstone FR and added land May 22 1902, added Teton and Absaroka reserves plus ~1 million new acres Jan 29 1903, and added more 1904, 1905 and Mar 2 1907; by 1908 Yellowstone FR was ~8.3 million acres before being split Jul 1 1908 (Shoshone created then). Washakie NF merged 1945.

units.earliest_reserve: Dismal River and Niobrara Forest Reserves
units.note: Dismal River, Niobrara (both Apr 16 1902) and North Platte (Mar 10 1906) combined as Nebraska NF Jul 2 1908. Niobrara division became Samuel R. McKelvie NF in 1971. Pine Ridge district lands came later (post-TR; verify).
Split from Nebraska NF by Act of Oct 15 1971.

units.earliest_reserve: White River Plateau Timber Land Reserve
units.primary_predecessor: White River Plateau Timber Land Reserve
units.note: TR re-described and renamed it White River Jun 28 1902 and added/deleted land May 21 1904. Holy Cross NF (Holy Cross FR Aug 25 1905, TR) merged 1945, a large TR-proclaimed addition.
TR added land to Black Mesa Jun 30 1906 and Jul 12 1907; Apache created Jul 1 1908 (EO 876) from Black Mesa; Mar 2 1909 added part of Crook. Datil NF land added 1925.
Created Jul 1 1908 (EO 868) from Black Mesa, which TR enlarged 1906-1907.

units.earliest_reserve: Grand Canon Forest Reserve (part combined into Coconino 1908)
units.note: Created Jul 2 1908 (Proc. 818) from San Francisco Mtns (1898; TR added land Apr 12 1902) plus parts of Black Mesa, Tonto and Grand Canyon reserves.

TR added land May 6 1905 and Aug 8 1906 (renamed Grand Canyon). North Kaibab created Jul 2 1908 (EO 909). Williams/Tusayan districts came via Tusayan NF (1910, from Coconino/San Francisco Mtns lineage). Large parts went to Grand Canyon NM (TR, 1908) and NP (1919).
TR added land Nov 26 1907 and merged Verde FR (Dec 30 1907) in 1908.

units.earliest_reserve: Black Mesa Forest Reserve (land added to Tonto 1908)
units.note: Tonto FR Oct 3 1905 + Pinal Mtns FR (Mar 20 1905) merged Jan 13 1908; land from Black Mesa (1898 reserve, enlarged by TR) added Jul 1 1908. Crook NF (Mt Graham 1902) part added 1953. Primary origin TR.

units.primary_predecessor: Santa Catalina / Santa Rita Forest Reserves
units.note: Coronado est. Jul 2 1908 from Santa Catalina (Jul 2 1902), Santa Rita (Apr 11 1902), Dragoon (1907); Garces (Baboquivari, Huachuca, Tumacacori 1906) added 1911; Chiricahua (Jul 30 1902) 1917; Crook (Mt Graham Jul 22 1902) 1953.
TR re-described and renamed it Gila Jul 21 1905 and added Big Burros FR (1907) Jun 18 1908. Datil NF lands added 1931, Crook 1953.
Alamo NF (Guadalupe and Sacramento reserves, 1907) merged 1917; Gallinas (1906) 1908.

units.earliest_reserve: Jemez Forest Reserve (part, via Carson EO 848/849)
units.note: Created Jun 26 1908 from Taos FR and part of Jemez; Mar 2 1909 added part of Jicarilla Apache lands. FS-612 records transfers from Santa Fe NF in 1923, 1950, 1962; Santa Fe includes Pecos River FR (1892) lineage, so a pre-TR fragment is possible - unverified.

units.primary_predecessor: Pecos River Forest Reserve + Jemez Forest Reserve
units.note: Pecos River was enlarged by McKinley (1898); FS-612 shows no TR addition to it (renamed Pecos 1908). Santa Fe NF formed Apr 6 1915 by combining Pecos with Jemez NF (Jemez FR Oct 12 1905, TR), so the modern forest contains a large TR-proclaimed share.

units.admin_unit: Cibola National Forest and National Grasslands
units.note: Manzano (Nov 6 1906), Mt Taylor (Oct 5 1906), Magdalena and San Mateo (Nov 5 1906) and Zuni (Mar 2 1909) all TR. Datil NF lands added 1931; Datil (1908) had absorbed part of Gila (1899) - possible pre-TR fragment in Magdalena district, unverified. National Grasslands (KS/OK/TX) are separate post-1930s units.
TR enlarged the Uintah reserve Jul 14 1905, Jan 16 1906 (renamed Uinta), Oct 6 1906; Ashley created Jul 1 1908 (EO 884) from it.

units.primary_predecessor: Uintah Forest Reserve; Payson FR (Aug 3 1901, McKinley) via Nebo NF
units.note: TR enlarged Uintah 1905-1906 and Payson Nov 5 1903 / Jul 21 1905. Payson + Vernon (1906) became Nebo NF 1908, merged into Uinta 1915.
Grantsville (May 7 1904) and Salt Lake (May 26 1904) added Jul 2 1908. Later transfers from Uinta (1915, 1929, 1935) carry Uintah 1897 lineage - possible pre-TR fragments.

units.primary_predecessor: Bear River Forest Reserve (from Logan FR)
units.note: Logan FR (May 29 1903) became Bear River 1906; remainder became Cache May 26 1908. Pocatello NF (Sep 5 1903) lands added 1915.
Caribou FR Jan 15 1907; Port Neuf (Mar 2 1907) via Pocatello; transfers from Cache 1939/1942 and Targhee 1961 (all TR-era lineage).

units.primary_predecessor: Henrys Lake FR + Idaho part of Yellowstone FR (Targhee est. Jul 1 1908)
units.note: Its Wyoming strip west of the Tetons came from Yellowstone FR; if any of it was in the original Teton FR (Feb 22 1897) the strict earliest would be pre-TR - unverified. Palisade NF (1910) returned 1917.

units.earliest_reserve: Yellowstone Forest Reserve expansion lands (Wyoming NF est. Jul 1 1908)
units.note: Wyoming NF was split from the Yellowstone FR, whose southern Wyoming extensions were added by TR (Jan 29 1903, May 4 1904, Mar 2 1907). Bonneville NF (1908) and first Bridger NF (1911) folded in. Earliest year depends on which Yellowstone proclamation first covered these ranges - verify (1903 assumed).
TR re-described Teton May 22 1902, merged it into Yellowstone FR Jan 29 1903 (with major additions), and re-established Teton NF Jul 1 1908.

units.primary_predecessor: Payette Forest Reserve (old) / Boise est. Jun 26 1908
units.note: Created Jun 26 1908 from parts of Payette (Jun 3 1905) and Sawtooth (May 29 1905); old Payette NF merged 1944.

units.primary_predecessor: Weiser + Idaho National Forests (new Payette Mar 18 1944)

units.earliest_reserve: Salmon River and Lemhi Forest Reserves
units.note: Lemhi NF divided between Salmon and Challis 1938.

units.primary_predecessor: Salmon River + Sawtooth Forest Reserves (Challis est. Jun 25 1908)

units.note: Minidoka NF (Cassia 1905 + Raft River 1906) merged 1953.
Sevier (May 12 1905) lands 1922; Powell NF (Aquarius FR Oct 24 1903) merged 1945.
TR added land May 2 1904, Jan 22 1906, Apr 29 1907, and Glenwood FR (1907) in 1908. Beaver/Fillmore (1906) lands added 1923.

units.primary_predecessor: Manti Forest Reserve; La Sal Forest Reserve (Jan 25 1906)
units.note: La Sal (incl. Monticello 1907) merged 1949; renamed Manti-La Sal 1950.

units.primary_predecessor: Ruby Mountains + Independence Forest Reserves (Humboldt est. Jul 2 1908)
units.note: Nevada NF (Feb 10 1909, TR) lands added 1957; Santa Rosa division (1911) post-TR.

units.earliest_reserve: Lake Tahoe Forest Reserve (via Tahoe NF transfer 1945) / possibly Sierra FR (via Mono NF)
units.note: Toiyabe FR proclaimed Mar 1 1907 (same days as the midnight reserves, but Nevada was not under the Fulton restriction). First Toiyabe merged into Nevada NF 1932 and re-established 1938. Spring Mountains via Moapa (Charleston FR Nov 5 1906). Received Mono NF lands (1910, 1945; Mono formed 1908 partly from Sierra FR of 1893) and Tahoe NF lands (1945; Lake Tahoe FR 1899). Primary origin TR.
TR added land Dec 23 1907; Angeles formed Jul 1 1908 from San Gabriel plus parts of San Bernardino and Santa Barbara.

units.primary_predecessor: San Bernardino FR (1893) and San Jacinto FR (1897)
units.note: Merged into Angeles 1908, re-established 1925 with San Jacinto lands from Cleveland. TR added land to San Jacinto Feb 14 1907 (and deleted from San Bernardino 1904).

units.primary_predecessor: Trabuco Canon (1893) + San Jacinto (1897) Forest Reserves
units.note: TR added land to San Jacinto Feb 14 1907 and to Trabuco Jul 6 1907; combined as Cleveland Jul 2 1908.

units.earliest_reserve: Pine Mountain and Zaca Lake Forest Reserve
units.primary_predecessor: Santa Barbara Forest Reserve (Dec 22 1903, from Pine Mtn/Zaca Lake and Santa Ynez)
units.note: TR combined the 1898/1899 reserves into Santa Barbara Dec 22 1903 and added land Oct 3 1906; Monterey (Jun 25 1906), San Luis Obispo (1906), Pinnacles and San Benito (1907) folded in 1908-1919. Renamed Los Padres 1936.
TR added land Feb 7 1905 (from Yosemite NP), Jul 25 1905, Jun 11 1906.

units.primary_predecessor: Sierra Forest Reserve (southern part; Sequoia est. Jul 2 1908)
units.note: Carved from the Sierra FR (which TR enlarged 1905-1906); TR added part of Tule River lands Mar 2 1909. Kern NF (1910) returned 1915.
TR added land Sep 7 1906 and Oct 26 1907, plus Sierra lands 1908. Calaveras Bigtree NF (authorized by Act of Feb 8 1909, signed by TR; established 1954) later folded in.
TR re-described/renamed it Tahoe Oct 3 1905 and added Yuba FR (Nov 11 1905) plus other land Sep 17 1906.

units.earliest_reserve: Lake Tahoe Forest Reserve (via Tahoe NF)
units.primary_predecessor: Tahoe National Forest (southern part; Eldorado est. Jul 28 1910 by Taft)
units.note: Created by Taft from Tahoe NF lands that include the 1899 Lake Tahoe reserve and TR's 1905-1906 Tahoe enlargements. Eldorado proclaimed post-TR, but its land base predates it.
Administrative unit (1973) assembled from Eldorado, Tahoe and Toiyabe NF lands in the basin; not a separately proclaimed NF.
Diamond Mtn (1905) lands 1907-1908. Received Tahoe NF lands 1910, 1921, 1965 (Lake Tahoe 1899 lineage) - possible pre-TR fragments.
Diamond Mtn (Jul 14 1905) remainder added 1908.

units.earliest_reserve: Modoc and Warner Mountains Forest Reserves

units.note: Received Crater NF land 1911 and Rogue River land 1948 (Ashland/Cascade Range 1893 lineage) - possible small pre-TR fragments.
Drawn by Elers Koch; signed by TR Oct 3 1905 (Davis 2022).
TR added part of Hoopa Valley lands Mar 2 1909.

units.primary_predecessor: Klamath, Siskiyou and Trinity National Forests (combined Jun 3 1947)
units.note: Established 1947 (Truman) entirely from TR-origin forests: Trinity 1905, Klamath 1905, Siskiyou 1906.

units.earliest_reserve: Trinity Forest Reserve (part via California NF)
units.primary_predecessor: Stony Creek Forest Reserve (Feb 6 1907) -> California NF (Jul 2 1908)
units.note: California NF formed from Stony Creek plus part of Trinity; renamed Mendocino 1932.

Inyo received Sierra NF land Jul 2 1908 and Mono NF lands 1945 (Mono partly from Sierra FR 1893). If those parcels were original 1893 Sierra reserve land, strict earliest would be pre-TR - unverified.
A Mar 1 1907 midnight reserve. Received Kaniksu NF land in Washington 1943 (Priest River FR 1897 lineage, possibly incl. TR's 1906/1907 additions) - possible pre-TR fragment.
TR added and deleted land in the Washington FR Jun 12 1905 and Mar 2 1907 (net change not computed).

units.earliest_reserve: Washington Forest Reserve / Mount Rainier Forest Reserve
units.primary_predecessor: Washington and Rainier Forest Reserves (Wenatchee est. Jul 1 1908)
units.note: TR enlarged both parents (Washington 1905, 1907; Rainier Mar 2 1907). Rainier NF lands added 1933.

units.earliest_reserve: Washington Forest Reserve / Mount Rainier Forest Reserve
units.primary_predecessor: Washington and Rainier Forest Reserves (Snoqualmie est. Jul 1 1908)

units.earliest_reserve: Mount Rainier Forest Reserve (which absorbed the 1893 Pacific FR)
units.primary_predecessor: Rainier FR -> Columbia NF (Jul 1 1908) -> Gifford Pinchot (1949)
units.note: TR enlarged Mt. Rainier FR Mar 2 1907 (renamed Rainier). The 1893 Pacific FR (Harrison) core is mostly in Mount Rainier NP, so 1897 is used as earliest. Renamed for Pinchot 1949.

McKinley deleted large areas 1900-1901; TR added land Mar 2 1907 and carved Mount Olympus NM from it (1909). Much later went to Olympic NP (1938-1943). FHS 1975 list misprints its date as Feb 22 1908.

units.primary_predecessor: Bull Run TLR (1892) + Cascade Range FR (1893) -> Oregon NF (1908) -> Mt. Hood (1924)
units.note: TR added land to Cascade Range Jan 25 1907 and Mar 2 1907 (renamed Cascade).

units.primary_predecessor: Cascade and Santiam National Forests (combined Apr 6 1933)
Cascade FR (part) + Blue Mtns FR (part) (Deschutes est. Jun 13 1908)
units.note: Includes TR-era Blue Mountains (1906) and Cascade additions (1907). Paulina NF lands 1915.

units.earliest_reserve: Cascade Range Forest Reserve (land added to Umpqua 1908)
units.note: Umpqua FR is a Mar 2 1907 midnight reserve; land from the Cascade FR (1893 lineage) was added Jun 30 1908, so strict earliest is pre-TR. Primary origin TR.

units.earliest_reserve: Cascade Range Forest Reserve / Ashland Forest Reserve
units.primary_predecessor: Ashland + Cascade FR lands -> Crater NF (Jun 30 1908) -> Rogue River (1932)
units.note: TR added land to Ashland Apr 24 1906 and Mar 2 1907, and to Cascade Range 1907.
Coquille FR (Mar 2 1907) added 1908. Exchanges with Crater/Rogue River (1911) could include small Ashland-lineage parcels - unverified.

units.primary_predecessor: Tillamook FR (+ part of Umpqua) -> Siuslaw (Jun 30 1908)
units.note: Tillamook is a midnight reserve.
Received Deschutes land Jul 14 1908, Paulina 1915, Deschutes 1933 (Cascade Range 1893 lineage possible) - unverified pre-TR fragments.

units.earliest_reserve: Cascade Range Forest Reserve (via Rogue River/Deschutes transfers, 1961)
units.primary_predecessor: Former Klamath Indian Reservation lands (Winema est. Jul 26 1961, Kennedy)
units.note: Majority of land is post-TR (former Klamath Reservation). Parts transferred from Rogue River and Deschutes NFs carry 1893/TR-era lineage. Recommend mapping as post-TR with a note.

units.primary_predecessor: Deschutes/Malheur NF lands (Ochoco est. Jun 30 1911, Taft)
units.note: Proclaimed by Taft, but land base came from TR-proclaimed Blue Mountains (1906) and Maury Mountain (1905) reserves via Deschutes and Malheur. If any former Cascade Range (1893) land via Deschutes is inside, strict earliest would change - unlikely, unverified.

units.primary_predecessor: Blue Mountains Forest Reserve (Malheur est. Jun 13 1908)
units.note: Blue Mountains FR absorbed part of Baker City FR (Feb 5 1904); whether that part went to Malheur or Whitman is unverified (1904 vs 1906).

units.primary_predecessor: Blue Mountains Forest Reserve (Whitman est. Jun 13 1908)
units.note: Minam NF (1911) returned 1920.

units.primary_predecessor: Heppner + Blue Mtns FR (Umatilla est. Jun 13 1908); Wenaha NF added 1920

units.note: Combined Jul 2 1908.

units.earliest_reserve: Afognak Forest and Fish Culture Reserve
units.note: Afognak (Harrison 1892) was merged into Chugach Jul 2 1908, so strict earliest is pre-TR. Much of Afognak Island has since passed out of federal forest status (ANCSA/later actions) - verify whether any Afognak acreage remains inside today's boundary. Primary origin TR (1907).

units.primary_predecessor: Luquillo Forest Reserve (renamed Caribbean NF 1935, El Yunque 2007)
units.note: Luquillo lands were a Spanish Crown forest reserve from 1876; first U.S. reservation was TR's proclamation of Jan 17 1903.
Oklahoma portion added later (1930s, post-TR). FS-612 OCR shows 'AR/OR' - Arkansas only in 1907.
St. Francis NF (1960) is post-TR.

Merged into Florida NF 1911 (with Choctawhatchee) and re-established as Ocala Oct 17 1927. Often called the oldest national forest east of the Mississippi (claim not verified here; Chippewa/Minnesota 1902 is older by act of Congress).

Lands transferred to the War Department by Act of Jun 27 1940 (now Eglin AFB). Davis 2022 still lists it '1927-Present', but it is unlikely to appear in USFS administrative-boundary data. Exclude from map or show as a historical footprint.

units.primary_predecessor: Minnesota National Forest (Act of May 23 1908; renamed Chippewa Jun 22 1928)
units.note: First federal forest reserve created by Congress rather than proclamation (FHS Highlights, 1902). FS-612 dates the Minnesota NF to Act of May 23 1908; the 1902 date is for the Morris Act reserve - verify exact 1902 act date (June 27, 1902 assumed).
Manistee NF (1938) is post-TR.
Included only because it shares an administrative unit with Huron.
